series.title: Student loans owned and securitized, quarter-end (G.19)
series.unit: billions of nominal US dollars, not seasonally adjusted
series.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, G.19 Consumer Credit, via FRED (series SLOASM)
series.notes: Quarter-end months (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec) of monthly FRED series SLOASM, updated 2026-11-06. Quarterly series SLOAS was discontinued after 2024Q4 (last value 1,777.1 bn); SLOASM continues it and carries revised values (2024Q4 = 1,778.4 bn). Covers federal and private student loans held by government, banks, finance companies and other lenders; includes nonfederal and federally held loans.

series.title: Student loans owned and securitized, constant September 2026 dollars
series.source_name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, G.19 Consumer Credit, via FRED (series SLOASM); deflated with BLS CPI-U (FRED CPIAUCSL)
series.notes: Analyst calculation: SLOASM quarter-end value times CPIAUCSL(2026-09 = 336.298) / CPIAUCSL(quarter-end month). CPI source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL

series.title: Student loan balances on consumer credit reports
series.source_name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit 2026Q3 (NY Fed Consumer Credit Panel/Equifax), data workbook
series.notes: Page 3 Data. Credit-report based (Equifax 5% panel), so differs from G.19 and FSA totals. NY Fed notes 2003-2004 balances may be undercounted due to servicer reporting lags. In 2025Q4 about one million borrowers 120+ days past due were transferred to ED's Default Resolution Group; NY Fed carried over their Q3 balance (2025Q4 PDF, https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/interactives/householdcredit/data/pdf/HHDC_2025Q4.pdf).

headline_facts.claim: Student loans owned and securitized (Federal Reserve G.19), end of September 2026
Student loan balances on credit reports, 2026Q3; up $5 billion (0.3%) from 2026Q2
Student loan balances grew from 2006Q1 to 2026Q3 in nominal terms (NY Fed); about 2.3x in constant September 2026 dollars ($0.73T to $1.66T, analyst CPI-U deflation)
In constant September 2026 dollars, credit-report student debt peaked in 2020Q2 at about $2.01 trillion and is now about 18% below that peak (analyst CPI-U deflation)
Share of student loan balances 90+ days delinquent, 2026Q3, up from 10.6% in 2026Q2
Share of student loan balances reported 90+ days delinquent in 2025Q1, the first quarter missed federal payments were again reported to credit bureaus, versus under 1% in 2024Q4
Annualized share of student loan balances transitioning into 90+ delinquency peaked in 2025Q4, then eased to 7.7% in 2026Q3

2026Q3 balances: auto loans $1.73T, student loans $1.66T, credit cards $1.29T; student loans exceeded auto loans in every quarter from 2010Q1 to 2023Q3 except 2023Q2, auto loans have been larger every quarter since 2023Q4, and student loans have exceeded credit cards every quarter since 2010Q2
Student loans as a share of total household debt, 2006Q1 vs 2026Q3 (analyst calculation)
Federal student loan portfolio, June 30, 2026 (FY2026 Q3): dollars outstanding and unduplicated recipients
Average federal student loan balance per borrower in 2026 dollars: 2007, 2020 peak, 2026 (March 31)
Federal Direct and ED-held FFEL loans in default (360+ days delinquent), June 30, 2026, per College Board from FSA data
2024-25 bachelor's recipients at public four-year institutions: share who borrowed and average debt per borrower (2025 dollars)
2024-25 bachelor's recipients at private nonprofit four-year institutions: share who borrowed and average debt per borrower (2025 dollars)
Share of public four-year bachelor's recipients who borrowed fell from 2014-15 to 2024-25 (private nonprofit: 63.4% to 50.0%)

caveats: Three totals measure different things: G.19 (all student loans held by lenders incl. federal government, $1.88T), FSA (federal loans only, principal plus interest, $1.72T), NY Fed (balances appearing on Equifax credit reports, $1.66T). Do not mix them on one line without labeling.

FRED SLOAS (quarterly) is discontinued; its last observation is 2024Q4. The live replacement is SLOASM (monthly, populated at quarter-end months through Sep 2026). SLOASM revises some history (2024Q4: 1,778.4 bn vs SLOAS 1,777.1 bn).
Constant-dollar series are analyst calculations using CPI-U (FRED CPIAUCSL, seasonally adjusted) with base September 2026 = 336.298. College Board series use its own 2025 or 2026 dollar adjustments.

NY Fed student loan delinquency for 2020Q2 to 2024Q4 is artificially low: missed federal payments were not reported to credit bureaus during the pandemic pause and the on-ramp period. The 2025 jump reflects resumed reporting, not a one-quarter collapse in repayment. Pre-2020 levels (about 11% 90+ in 2019Q4) are the fair comparison.
NY Fed flow (transition) rates are 4-quarter moving sums, so they lag and smooth quarter-to-quarter changes.
In 2025Q4 about one million borrowers 120+ days past due were transferred to ED's Default Resolution Group and reported zero balances; NY Fed carried over their Q3 balance and status (2025Q4 report).

FSA counts unduplicated 'recipients' (the student who benefited); for Parent PLUS the parent is the borrower. FSA fiscal quarters: Q1 ends Dec 31, Q2 Mar 31, Q3 Jun 30, Q4 Sep 30. FSA's earliest year is FY2007; the FY2026 Q4 (Sep 30, 2026) update was not yet posted.

College Board bachelor's debt figures cover only public and private nonprofit four-year schools, only students who started at the school they graduated from, exclude Parent PLUS, and are reported for selected years (2009-10, 2014-15, 2019-20, 2024-25) in 2025 dollars.
NY Fed credit-report data in 2003-2004 may undercount student loans due to servicer reporting lags; series here start at 2006Q1.
NY Fed changed the credit score used on origination pages to VantageScore 4.0 from 2026Q1; this does not affect the balance or delinquency series used here.
unconfirmed: NCES data: not opened; no NCES figures used.

FSA loan status / delinquency workbooks (PortfolioByLoanStatus.xls, DLPortfolioByDelinquencyStatus.xls) returned 404 at the guessed URLs; default figures come instead from College Board Trends in Student Aid 2026 Fig SA-13A, which cites the FSA Data Center.
Official FSA cohort default rates and any ED statements on wage garnishment or Treasury offset after collections restarted: not retrieved.
